title: A program in a pane cannot tell agents which verbs it accepts
body:
`scratch.send` takes `verb` and `payload`, and decade sends `{"to": "<scratch pane>", "<verb>": payload}` to the program in the scratch pane (`docs/protocol.md`, "Agents: MCP"). A program declares the kinds it shows in its hello (`Hello` in `decade-channel`), and `panes` lists them. No program declares the verbs it accepts beyond those kinds. An agent that opens a program in the scratch pane has no way to learn what to send it, other than reading the program's source.

## Proposal

A program lists the verbs it accepts in its hello, each with a line of description, and `panes` returns them beside `shows`. The `scratch.send` description tells the agent to look there.

## Cost

`Hello` and `Pane` gain a field. `decade-channel` moves its minor version, and `decade` moves its minor for the protocol change.

## Open

- Whether a verb also declares the shape of its payload, as a JSON schema, or only names it.
close_reason: Landed in da4f5cd: accepts entries take a bare name or a name with a description, and panes returns them.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/7403d304
notes.text: Jack decided: a program lists each verb it accepts by name with one sentence of description. No payload schema.
